title: Meerut cops face action after ‘torture’ charge against farm leader, Dalit associate
content: Several Meerut police officers were recalled after a farmer leader alleged torture in custody.  An inquiry was ordered by the ADG, Meerut zone, into the serious allegations.  The farmer leader claimed he and his associate were assaulted for hours by senior officers.  Police initially denied the claims but later deleted their statement from social media.  Authorities have now attached the SSP to state headquarters in Lucknow for further action.

title: After Maharashtra hill tragedy, Delhi man jumps into Yamuna over iPhone
content: A dance teacher jumped into the Yamuna river in Delhi due to financial stress. Deepak Kumar, a resident of Okhla, faced difficulties paying his iPhone installments. Police personnel on patrol alerted the flood department after spotting the man. A rescue team arrived quickly and brought the man safely to shore. Kumar was counseled and sent home after his family arrived at the station.

title: From Thumba to tomorrow: Indian space programme is preparing for its biggest leap yet
content: India's space program began with a small rocket range in 1962.  It progressed to launching its first satellite and developing indigenous launch vehicles.  Chandrayaan-3's lunar landing marked a significant achievement for the nation.  The program now includes private sector involvement and ambitious future goals.  India aims for a space station by 2035 and a lunar landing by 2040.

title: Shubman Gill joins Sachin Tendulkar, Virender Sehwag in elite Test list
content: Shubman Gill marked a remarkable achievement by crossing the 3,000 Test run milestone, becoming the fourth-youngest Indian cricketer to do so. This significant moment took place on the inaugural day of the second Test, as he eclipsed the record previously held by former skipper Kapil Dev. The milestone was particularly notable, considering it followed a gradual and measured start to his innings.

title: Hindu family of four found dead in Bangladesh’s Rangpur; strangulation suspected
content: A chilling scene unfolded when police discovered the bodies of four members of a Hindu family in their locked home. Initial investigations point to strangulation and a possible robbery. The family's absence since Thursday and the lack of phone activity raised alarm. Following a forced entry, officers located the victims throughout the house. Autopsy results are pending to establish the precise cause of their untimely deaths.

title: Why ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt is 'unhappy' with his former boss Sergey Brin
content: Eric Schmidt has expressed discontent regarding Sergey Brin's financial backing for political measures, which includes a staggering $100 million aimed at challenging California's Proposition 40. His irritation is exacerbated by investments in various ballot initiatives, particularly a wealth tax that impacts individuals boasting a net worth exceeding $1 billion. The former Google CEO is determined to thwart this proposed tax targeting billionaires.

title: ‘Unacceptable’: Langer slams two-day Tests after Australia rout Bangladesh
content: Justin Langer, the former Australian opener, has voiced strong concerns about the troubling rise of Test matches ending in just two days. He argues that this phenomenon could jeopardise the sport's integrity and financial viability, attributing it to fundamental weaknesses in batting skills and footwork. Bangladesh's captain, Najmul Hossain Shanto, acknowledged the tough conditions and emphasised the importance of gaining more international experience.

title: Microsoft has a 6-word answer for students wondering if coding is still worth it
content: Microsoft Learn has told students on X that learning to code is worth it "now more than ever", even as AI writes a growing share of software. Satya Nadella says AI already produces up to 30% of Microsoft's code, while Google puts its figure at 75%. The skill has not died, it has shifted from writing syntax to reviewing, debugging and directing AI-generated code.

title: Torso in suitcase: Victim is Tamil woman, police hunt on for Odia couple
content: Police identified Haidul Nisha, a woman whose torso was found in a suitcase.  A couple from Odisha has been identified as suspects in this case.  CCTV footage showed the couple carrying the suitcase to Chennai Central station.  The train departed Chennai on August 5 and arrived in Agra on August 6.  Special teams are currently tracking the suspects' mobile signals to apprehend them.

title: Apollo 15 brought back green glass beads; decades later they revealed lunar water
content: Apollo 15 astronauts found unusual green flecks on the Moon's surface. These flecks were later identified as volcanic glass beads containing trapped water. Researchers discovered hydrogen within these tiny beads, proving lunar water existed. This finding challenged the long-held belief that the Moon was extremely dry. The discovery revealed significant water presence deep within the Moon's interior.

title: 'Everyone should take time in quiet': Melinda Gates on divorce and life changes
content: Melinda French Gates advocates for self-care during significant life changes. She learned this lesson during early motherhood and her divorce from Bill Gates. French Gates advises taking quiet time daily for personal reflection and wellness. She believes processing transitions helps individuals learn and grow from experiences. This approach supports mental health and work-life balance for everyone.

title: US FTA proposal: What are the '3 American demands' that became deal breaker for Canada
content: In a significant turn of events, Canada has halted trade negotiations with the United States due to unresolved disagreements. Three critical demands from the US regarding Canada's auto industry and trade agreements proved too contentious. Additionally, restrictions concerning language and culture were deemed unacceptable. As a result, both nations are now enacting retaliatory tariffs on each other's products.

title: Maha hill tragedy: New video shows mother kneeling before son, begging him to step back
content: A tragic scene unfolded at Khavdya Dongar when a teenager jumped to his death, despite his mother's heartfelt pleas, where she knelt in an attempt to save him. Villagers and police labored for over three hours to reach him, but as his father tried to pull him back, calamity struck, resulting in the loss of both parents during this devastating fall.

title: Queens bucks the trend: New apartments grow bigger despite NYC’s space crunch
content: Queens saw new apartments increase in size over the last decade.  This growth outpaced the national average for apartment size gains.  Brooklyn and Manhattan apartments, however, became smaller during this same period.  Developers in high-demand areas often prioritize smaller units for more availability.  The average US apartment size has increased overall, but Queens remains smaller.

title: Hockey WC: How can India qualify for the semifinals? The permutations explained
content: Despite the setback against the Netherlands, India's aspirations for the Hockey World Cup semifinal are still alive, albeit slim. With Argentina's win against England, Craig Fulton's team now has a chance, needing a decisive victory over Argentina by at least two goals. Additionally, a significant win by the Netherlands against England is crucial for India to progress based on goal difference metrics.

title: Ugly scenes! Jaiswal, Fernando clash after heated send-off in Colombo - Watch
content: Emotions ran high as Yashasvi Jaiswal and Asitha Fernando clashed following the dismissal of the Indian opener. Fernando's exuberant celebration sparked a fiery exchange, necessitating the intervention of the Sri Lankan captain to defuse the situation. By the end of the morning session, India found themselves at 88/2 after winning the toss, maintaining a lead of 1-0 in the two-match Test series following their previous win.

title: Delhi: Cab driver, wife & son held for killing passenger over fare dispute
content: A cab driver, his wife, and son were arrested for murder.  They allegedly killed a passenger after a fare dispute escalated.  The victim was found naked with severe injuries near a wall.  Police identified the vehicle and apprehended the family members.  Evidence was recovered, and the victim's identity is still unknown.

title: Anti-quota protests: Chirag Paswan says govt open to talks if demands set systematically
content: Union minister Chirag Paswan has signaled that the government plans to engage with the anti-reservation protesters who have rallied at Jantar Mantar. These protesters are advocating for an economic basis for reservations rather than a caste-based system. Paswan noted the existing 10 percent reservation for economically weaker sections and criticized the Congress for their protests outside a police station. Tejashwi Yadav’s backing of students' protests aligns with his political stance.

title: Mitchell Starc makes history! Enters record books to leave Bumrah trailing
content: Mitchell Starc has clinched his fourth Player of the Series accolade after achieving a remarkable 10-wicket haul. This outstanding performance not only highlights his exceptional skill but also elevates him above Dale Steyn on the all-time wicket-takers leaderboard. Starc has gained these series awards across three nations, alongside notable pacers like Jasprit Bumrah and Pat Cummins. Australia is set to embark on a grueling twelve-month stint featuring twenty Test matches.

title: Revanth planned to meet Vance, Mamdani on US trip that MEA denied nod to

The ministry stated the proposed program was inappropriate for the CM's official visit.  Revanth Reddy is currently in the United Kingdom, meeting educational institutions.  His deputy called the denial of permission unfortunate and politically motivated.

title: ‘Canada wants benefits of being State’: Trump's 1st reaction after trade talks collapse
content: In a significant turn of events, Canada has halted trade discussions with the United States due to last-minute demands deemed unreasonable. In retaliation, President Donald Trump has reignited his '51st state' comments while imposing tariffs. The US negotiation team mentioned that Canada declined to accept a tariff reduction proposal on critical products.

title: Rajiv Thakur's father passes away; Krushna Abhishek informs fans

Consequently, their upcoming performance has been canceled. Attendees are advised to be aware of this change. Many are sending their heartfelt condolences to Rajiv and his family during this difficult time.

title: Before AI, there was the Mechanical Turk: The chess machine that wasn’t
content: The Mechanical Turk first appeared in 1770 as a chess-playing machine that astonished audiences across Europe and the Americas. It played Benjamin Franklin and Napoleon Bonaparte, but the secret was a skilled chess player hidden inside its cabinet. Despite widespread suspicion, the illusion endured for decades. Its story offers a striking reminder that the impression of an autonomous mind can hide the reality behind it.

title: Meet John Liu, the student who used corn stalks to recover lithium from water
content: John Liu has pioneered a remarkable project that utilizes agricultural byproducts like corn stalks and wheat straw to innovate lithium recovery methods. His technique leverages plant-based scaffolds to effectively concentrate lithium from dilute brines. Through his groundbreaking work, Liu garnered accolades at both state and international science fairs, showcasing a sustainable pathway for reclaiming essential battery materials and underscoring the role of agricultural waste in advancing environmental engineering solutions.

title: Delhi cops attacked with bricks, sticks, chilli powder during patrol; teen held

This confrontation occurred after police seized a motorcycle lacking valid documents.  One 17-year-old juvenile was apprehended, while other attackers fled the scene.  Authorities are actively searching for the main absconding accused, Sunil alias Pankaj.

title: No problem with boys but PM gets ‘cultural shock’ if girls use cuss words: Rahul

Gandhi invoked Manusmriti, asserting women belong only to themselves. He highlighted that examination paper leaks affect women differently due to marriage pressures. The Congress leader invited students to share their experiences of harassment and educational challenges.

The day aims to inspire greater interest in science and technology for all.

title: 'I fought cancer to see my son play for India': Saransh's long road to Test cricket
